industry_fit.rationale: 3M is a direct competitor manufacturing protective films and overlaminates for the exact same applications as Tedlar. Their Graphics & Signage division produces films for vehicle wraps (3M Wrap Film Series 2080, IJ280), building graphics and wraps (Controltac, Scotchcal films), architectural panels (DI-NOC Architectural Finishes), signs and displays, and transit applications. They manufacture overlaminates including anti-graffiti products (8588G, 8590M) specifically designed to protect graphics from vandalism, scratches, and UV damage—identical use cases to Tedlar's protective films.

size_revenue_fit.rationale: 3M is a Fortune 500 multinational conglomerate with $24.95 billion in annual revenue (FY2025) and 61,500 employees globally as of December 2024. The company operates in over 70 countries with operations across multiple continents. As one of the world's largest diversified technology companies, 3M far exceeds the $100M+ revenue and 500+ employee thresholds, representing the upper end of the target company profile.

strategic_relevance.rationale: While 3M's products serve identical applications, they are a direct competitor rather than a customer prospect. 3M manufactures their own protective overlaminates with 8-9 year outdoor durability claims (Scotchcal 8518/8519 series), comprehensive MCS warranties, and established anti-graffiti solutions. Their wrap films already feature warranties up to 8 years vertical exposure. As a materials science company with 60+ years in the graphics industry, 3M would be sourcing their own fluoropolymer or alternative protective technologies rather than purchasing Tedlar films as an input material.

market_activity.rationale: 3M demonstrates exceptional market presence in the graphics and signage industry. They are referenced as exhibitors and technology providers at major industry events including ISA Sign Expo and PRINTING United. Recent activity includes showcasing their building wrap at their St. Paul headquarters (2018 project with Vomela Companies) and launching new products like the Protection Wrap Film Color Series (2024 promotion running through December). The company maintains comprehensive warranty programs (3M MCS Warranty) and extensive installer training networks, indicating deep industry engagement and leadership position.

qualification_summary: 3M Commercial Solutions is NOT a qualified prospect for Tedlar protective films. While 3M perfectly matches the industry vertical and company size criteria as a $25B Fortune 500 manufacturer in graphics/signage/vehicle wraps, they are a direct competitor producing their own protective overlaminates and films with similar durability claims (8-9 years outdoor). 3M would be developing competitive protective technologies rather than purchasing Tedlar films, making this a competitive intelligence target rather than a sales opportunity.
